properties.natural_language: Before activating a new blob parameter schedule, the epoch must be >= the scheduled activation epoch in BLOB_SCHEDULE
Before validating blob commitment count, the number of blob_kzg_commitments must be compared against the epoch-specific max_blobs_per_block limit
Before shifting proposer lookahead window, the first epoch's proposer indices must be removed to maintain the sliding window
After blob parameter lookup, if no scheduled entry applies, the system must fallback to MAX_BLOBS_PER_BLOCK_ELECTRA
After block receives more blob commitments than allowed for current epoch, the block must be rejected
After proposer lookahead update, get_beacon_proposer_index must perform O(1) lookup using state.proposer_lookahead[state.slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH]
After computing fork digest with blob parameters, the digest must be XORed with hash(epoch + max_blobs_per_block)[:4] to ensure network partition on blob schedule changes
All nodes on the network must agree on BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration to ensure consistent fork digest computation and prevent unintentional network partition
Proposer lookahead must be computed deterministically from beacon state so all honest nodes agree on proposer assignments
Blob schedule epoch thresholds must be set far enough in advance for all nodes to upgrade before activation to prevent chain splits
Before wallet_sendCalls request processing, the request schema must be validated including version, chainId format, and call objects structure
Before accepting batched calls, if app-provided ID exists, it must be unique for this sender per application
Before executing atomic batch, if atomicRequired=true, wallet must verify it can execute all calls atomically or reject with error 5760
At the application-wallet boundary, when DApp submits wallet_sendCalls, the wallet must validate all required capabilities are supported before prompting user
At the application-wallet boundary, wallet_getCapabilities must check authorization before returning capability information to prevent fingerprinting
After user rejects batched calls, the wallet must return error 4001 (user rejected) to the application
After user approves calls, wallet must generate unpredictable unique batch identifier before returning to application
After batch execution completes, status must transition to 200 (all success), 500 (all failed), or 600 (partial failure) based on individual call results
After untrusted caller queries capabilities, wallet must filter sensitive capabilities to prevent fingerprinting attacks
Applications must correctly report their identity when making requests to prevent impersonation and unauthorized batch status access
Wallet implementations must correctly enforce call ordering as specified in the request to prevent security issues in dependent operations
Users must understand the difference between atomic and non-atomic execution when approving requests to prevent unexpected partial execution
Before processing wallet_getCallsStatus for a batch ID, wallet should return error 5730 if the ID is from a different application to prevent cross-application information leakage
Before speed-up validation, replacement transaction must have same nonce, recipient, value, and data as original, with gas price increased by at least 10%
Before cancelling transaction, replacement transaction must be constructed with same nonce, from=to (self-send), value=0, and data=empty

Before emitting replacement event, provider must classify replacement type by comparing transaction fields: speed-up (same fields), cancel (self-send pattern), or generic replacement (only nonce matches)
After speed-up transaction is submitted, provider must emit tx_speedup event with oldTx, newTx, nonce, and from address
After cancel transaction is submitted, provider must emit tx_cancel event to notify DApp of cancellation attempt
After generic replacement is submitted, provider must emit tx_replacement event when fields differ beyond just gas price
Replacement transaction must be submitted before original is mined, otherwise replacement will fail and event semantics become unclear
Wallet/provider must correctly track pending transactions and their nonces to detect replacements accurately
Only the transaction sender can replace their own transaction to prevent transaction censorship or manipulation by attackers
Before MODEXP execution, length parameters (base_length, exp_length, modulus_length) must be extracted from first 96 bytes as big-endian uint256
Before computing MODEXP gas cost, exponent head (first 32 bytes of exponent with zero-padding if shorter) must be extracted for iteration calculation
Before MODEXP calculation, if modulus equals zero, the result must be zero bytes of length modulus_length without performing exponentiation
After MODEXP computation, result must be padded to modulus_length bytes as big-endian encoding
After gas calculation, the final cost must be max(200, (complexity * iterations) / 3) where complexity = ((max(base_length, modulus_length) + 7) // 8)^2
After input validation, if base_length and modulus_length are both zero, empty result must be returned
Python's pow(base, exp, modulus) function must correctly implement modular exponentiation with constant-time behavior to prevent timing side-channel attacks
Gas cost formula must accurately reflect computational complexity to prevent DoS attacks through computationally expensive modexp calls
Minimum gas cost of 200 must be sufficient to prevent spam attacks using trivial modexp calls
Before processing input shorter than declared lengths, zero-padding must be applied for missing bytes consistent with EVM memory semantics
Before transitioning EIP from draft to post-draft status, version must be updated from 0.x.x to 1.0.0
Before merging PR that modifies EIP specification, commit message must contain scope indicator ([Mm]ajor:, [Mm]inor:, or [Pp]atch:)
Before version increment, if multiple scope indicators exist in commits, the most severe scope must be selected (major > minor > patch)
After PR is approved, changelog entry must be generated with version, date, PR number, and description
After version increment, both the version header field and CHANGELOG section must be updated in the EIP markdown
EIP authors must understand and correctly apply semantic versioning principles to prevent incorrect version increments causing compatibility misinterpretation
Commit message discipline must be maintained across all PR submissions to ensure proper version tracking
Before determining PATCH scope, cosmetic changes must be defined as formatting, typos, grammar, or documentation improvements without technical specification changes
Before activating fork based on block number, current block number must be >= ByBlockNumber activation threshold
Before activating fork based on timestamp, current timestamp must be >= ByTimestamp activation threshold for post-merge forks
Before selecting applicable fork, forks must be ordered with BLOCK_NUMBER forks first, then TIMESTAMP forks, then UNSCHEDULED using tuple comparison
At the network boundary, when block is received from peer, fork criteria must be evaluated to select correct validation rules
After fork criteria check for Unscheduled fork, check() must always return False (Literal[False]) preventing activation on mainnet
After fork rules are determined for a block, the specific validation rules must be applied from the identified fork
All nodes in the network must agree on fork activation thresholds to prevent chain splits from disagreeing on block validity
Block timestamps must be reasonably accurate and cannot be arbitrarily manipulated to prevent premature or delayed fork activations
Fork activation thresholds must be set correctly by protocol developers and cannot be changed without consensus to prevent unintended activations
Before Constantinople fork activation, block number must be >= network-specific fork block (Mainnet=7,280,000, Ropsten=4,230,000, Kovan=9,200,000, Rinkeby=3,660,663)
Before validating block, network must be identified to determine which fork block threshold applies
At the network boundary, when block is received from peer, correct ruleset (Byzantium or Constantinople) must be selected based on block height comparison
After fork block is reached, all 5 EIPs (145, 1014, 1052, 1234, 1283) must activate atomically at the same block without intermediate states
After Constantinople activation, the rule change is permanent and irreversible unless a reorg moves chain tip below fork block
All client implementations must correctly implement fork block numbers for each network to prevent chain splits from disagreeing on fork timing
Node operators must upgrade software before fork block is reached to prevent non-upgraded nodes from forking onto minority chain
Before executing opcode, the opcode byte must be fetched at evm.code[evm.pc] and decoded to valid Ops enum value
Before message call processing, depth must be validated against STACK_DEPTH_LIMIT (1024) to prevent stack overflow
Before contract creation, address collision must be checked using account_has_code_or_nonce() to prevent overwriting existing contracts
After ExceptionalHalt exception, all gas must be consumed (gas_left = 0), output must be cleared, and error must be set
After Revert exception, remaining gas must be preserved, output retained, error set, and transaction state rolled back
After contract creation, code starting with 0xEF prefix must be rejected per EIP-3541 to reserve prefix for EOF format
After contract creation, code size must not exceed MAX_CODE_SIZE (0x6000 = 24576 bytes) or creation fails
After execution complete, final refund must be calculated as min(accumulated_refund, gas_used/5) per refund cap
Transient storage in message.tx_env must be properly isolated per transaction and cleared between transactions to prevent cross-transaction leakage
The evm_trace function must have no side effects on execution state to prevent tracing from causing non-deterministic execution
Before MODEXP precompile accepts input, all three length parameters (base, exponent, modulus) must be <= 1024 bytes (8192 bits)
At the precompile boundary, when caller invokes MODEXP at address 0x05, input length validation must occur before complex processing
After length limit violation detected, all available gas must be consumed and error status must be returned to caller
After all length validations pass, MODEXP calculation must proceed with standard EIP-198 computation logic
Bounded inputs create a finite and testable input space, enabling comprehensive testing to prevent consensus bugs
Bounded inputs enable future replacement of MODEXP with EVM code via EVMMAX, improving auditability and consensus safety
Historical blockchain analysis accurately represents all legitimate MODEXP use cases, ensuring 1024-byte limit does not break existing applications
All client implementations must correctly implement bounds check identically to prevent consensus failures that EIP-7823 aims to prevent
Before Whisper message exchange, both peers must complete status message (0x00) handshake with version, PoW requirement, and optional bloom filter
Before envelope acceptance, envelope must pass structure validation, PoW verification (not NaN, INF, or negative), and bloom filter match
At the application-network boundary, plaintext message must be encrypted with ECIES or AES-GCM, signed with ECDSA, and padded to 256-byte alignment before transmission
At the P2P boundary, when envelope is received from peer, it must undergo validation before being processed or forwarded
After envelope validation fails, envelope must be silently dropped without notification to sender
After severe protocol violation detected, peer must be disconnected to prevent further misbehavior
After encryption, message must be padded to prevent size-based metadata leakage using 256-byte alignment
Attackers cannot break ECIES or AES-GCM encryption within message TTL timeframe to maintain confidentiality
Bloom filter must provide sufficient privacy to hide exact topic interests and prevent traffic analysis attacks
Sufficient network peers must exist to provide anonymity through message mixing and prevent timing analysis attacks
Before processing unknown packet codes, malformed packets (invalid encoding) should be rejected, but unknown valid packet codes should be silently ignored
